reviews.classification: dated setup/research plan with explicit correction and unmeasured platform limits
reviews.disposition: ER10-F1–F15, C1–C6, R1–R9, A1–A5 and N1 are dated source research with no measured browser timing, retention, eviction or gameplay run. Capability, browser/OS version, normal/private or installed mode, returned permission result and actual policy are distinct evidence. Preserve engine-specific unknowns and contradictions rather than applying Chromium timer or lock rules to Safari/Firefox/Edge. The report qualifies Safari use-day interaction versus calendar-day absence and records persistence/ITP contrary evidence; a closed unmerged proposal is not a shipped fix. Numeric quota ceilings are not reserved free bytes; localStorage differs from origin IDB/OPFS, which does not bypass eviction. Lock queries may affect cached holders in the documented historical Chromium implementation, so a probe is not automatically harmless observation. One held lock does not prove every legacy mutation guarded or real duplicate-writer loss. Lifecycle save/reacquire, monotonic awake versus capped absence, hidden visual cleanup, stable causal IDs and optional bounded codec are consumer proposals, not a selected offline policy. Cross-engine pow/Intl differences are possible, not measured outcomes here; platform availability/versions require fresh checks before adoption. Current AD39 and desktop targets supersede old host/viewport assumptions; no runtime, storage, browser or power policy changed.
